newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FELLOW PLAYERS HAPPY TO SEE DALY BACK IN FORM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FELLOW PLAYERS HAPPY TO SEE DALY BACK IN FORM.

text.p: Firmer conditions at Winged Foot could shake up the leaderboard on Friday, but for one day at least, John Daly and his amazing return was the talk of the PGA Championship.
"It's great to see him not only shoot a great number in a major, but to see him come back, because he hasn't played that much golf since he's been back," Tiger Woods said.
Daly, who missed the Masters and British Open after undergoing treatment for his alcoholism, shared the first-round lead with Davis Love by shooting a record-tying round of four-under-par 66.
Masters champion Woods, who shot an even-par 70 in the first round, said he and playing partners Ernie Els (70) and Justin Leonard (68) had been rooting for Daly.

"For him to go out there and have the guts to do that and shoot a good number like that, that takes a lot of courage," Woods said. "Ernie and Justin and myself were talking about it and we're very proud of him for doing that."
The long-hitting Daly has the 1991 PGA title and 1995 British Open crown to his credit, while Love is seeking his first major championship, but Daly was the major surprise.

Looking fitter since going on a diet and exercise regimen following his treatment, Daly made a spectacular return to major championship golf. He was last seen walking off the course midway through the second round of the U.S. Open in June because of a bad case of the shakes.
"Actually I was more impressed with his drives than his weight and his personal looks," Paul Azinger laughed after being asked about the new-look Daly. "He's not my kind of guy."
Azinger was in a threesome with Daly on Wednesday. He shot a 68 himself, as did another former PGA champion, Bob Tway, who rounded out the group.
"Actually he does look good and you can tell he's very competitive right now," Azinger said.
"I think that there was a time when he wasn't as competitive, where he kind of was going through the motions more than anything and really didn't care, and you don't see that in him right now.

Friday, of course, is another day and the warm and sunny conditions in the forecast should dry the course and make it harder for the 150-man field to keep tee shots in the fairway and out of the rough, and to hold approach shots on Winged Foot's small, elevated greens.
That does not mean that Daly will be a one-round wonder.
"He looks good and he's swinging good and he seems happy and it's great to see him playing good," Love said. "He's good for the game the way he is right now.
"I think if he keeps playing this way, he's going to be right back in the winner's circle real soon because he's extremely talented.
"When he putts good -- just like Tiger -- when they putt good, they ought to win."
